Subject: Security intake: vulnerability management, pen test & SOC 2 scope

Hi Terry —

Great to meet yesterday. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on what Acme needs from a security/compliance perspective to evaluate Redwood:

Summary of asks from your team:
- SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) and date of last audit
- HIPAA support / BAA availability (we offer Private deployments + options)
- GDPR data-processing details for EU users (data residency & deletion)
- Initiate vendor security questionnaire (you mentioned a short security intake form)
- Pen test report or proof of engagement and our vulnerability management SLAs/cadence

What we’ll send you by EOD tomorrow (attachments and links below):
- Draft SOW for our pen test intake and proposed scope (external-facing summary + contractor handoff) [attachment: Redwood_PenTest_SOW.pdf]
- Vulnerability disclosure and remediation policy (how we triage & publicly disclose CVEs) [attachment: Vuln_Disclosure_Policy.txt]
- Proposed SLA matrix and scanning cadence (critical/high/medium time-to-remediate) [attachment: SLA_and_Scan_Cadence.xlsx]

Immediate next steps:
1) Please confirm the primary technical contact for your security team (cc’d security-eng@acme-health.com is fine).
2) If you want us to complete your vendor questionnaire, drop the doc or a link and we’ll prioritize it.
3) Let us know 2x 30-minute windows for a technical deep-dive next week (we’ll include David for architecture).

Thanks — we’ll be responsive to any items that impact procurement or timelines.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

Hannah —

Thanks for the recap and for sending the attachments. A few clarifications from our side before we schedule the call:

1) SOC 2: we’ll need the most recent SOC 2 Type II report and a summary of any exceptions noted in the last audit.
2) HIPAA: Acme is handling PHI for certain workflows. Do you have an existing BAA template? If Redwood supports HIPAA, we’ll need confirmation of covered controls and any limitations (e.g., hosted vs private).
3) Pen test: we don’t require that you share raw findings publicly, but we do need a redacted executive summary from the most recent third-party pen test and the cadence of third-party assessments.
4) Vulnerability SLA: please provide your standard remediation SLAs for Critical/High/Medium findings and your process for notifying customers when a public exploit exists.

We’ve uploaded our questionnaire to the shared drive; link below. If you can assign someone from your security or engineering team to fill the technical sections, that would speed procurement.

Link: https://acme-health.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/security/QA-Redwood-Intake

Technical contact for Acme: security-eng@acme-health.com
Procurement contact: procurement@acme-health.com

Best,
Terry Mills

Acme Health

Subject: Re: Security intake: vulnerability management, pen test & SOC 2 scope

Terry —

Thanks for the quick reply and the SharePoint link. I’m looping in a couple of details that typically address the procurement/security checklist items you called out:

SOC 2
- We completed a SOC 2 Type II audit in May 2026; final report available. We will provide a redacted copy to protect sensitive findings and customer identities.

HIPAA / BAA
- Redwood supports HIPAA-covered deployments via our Private offering; we have a standard BAA template and can produce a scope addendum for on-prem or VPC deployments.

Pen test & cadence
- Third-party pentest: annual engagement with a CREST-certified provider; last engagement completed Aug 2026.
- Internal automated scans: weekly authenticated SAST/DAST and daily dependency vulnerability checks.
- Proposed cadence for joint engagements: full external pentest annually, targeted retests for major releases or public exploit exposure.

Vulnerability SLAs (proposed / typical)
- Critical: initial acknowledgement within 4 hours, mitigation or hotfix within 48 hours where feasible.
- High: acknowledgement within 8 hours, remediation within 7 calendar days.
- Medium: acknowledgement within 24 hours, remediation within 30 days.
- We apply risk-based exceptions for legacy infra that requires migration planning; those are tracked and communicated via ticket.

Disclosure & communication
- If a public exploit exists, we notify affected customers within 24 hours of verification and publish an advisory to our security status portal.
- We provide redacted executive summaries of third-party penetration tests and an internal remediation plan for critical findings.

Next steps I recommend:
1) We’ll fill the technical sections of your SharePoint questionnaire by EOD tomorrow (Hannah/David will own technical answers).
2) Attach SOW and SLA docs for your review (see attachments).
3) Propose a 30-minute call Thursday 11/19 at 10:00 AM PT to walk the technical team through scope and timeline.

David will follow up with architecture-level notes on tokenization and data flows for PHI in sandbox vs production.

—
Sergio Alvarez
VP, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com

Sergio / Hannah —

Appreciate the clarity — that SLA matrix looks good as a starting point. A couple follow-ups before the call:

- Please include a redacted SOC 2 report (we need to confirm there are no control exceptions related to encryption, access controls, and change management).
- For HIPAA, please share your BAA template so our legal team can review.
- On cadence: for Acme we prefer annual third-party pentests but require retests within 30 days for critical findings. Can Redwood commit to that retest window?

If you can send the redacted SOC2 and BAA by EOD Wednesday, we can keep procurement on track for a December procurement review.

Thanks,
Terry
